author: AlexanderKalistratov
title: Windows CC build fails with compiler out-of-heap-space errors under high parallelism

root_cause: The Windows Conditional Compilation build compiles many large MSVC projects (onednn/dnnl_cpu_x64, openvino_runtime, frontends/common, lp_transformations, core/reference) in parallel via MSBuild/cl.exe. Each cl.exe invocation attempting excessive internal compiler parallelism (/cgthreads) combined with many concurrent MSBuild project builds exhausts the 32-bit MSVC front-end's heap, producing cascading C1060 'compiler is out of heap space' and D8027 errors across nearly every object file once the first one is hit. This matches a known recurring runner-capacity/parallelism issue (pattern 80cfa127185fbf3e), already observed 26 times since 2026-11-03, rather than a new code regression; no source change in the triggering commit is implicated.
reproduction_steps: N/A - this is an environment/resource-exhaustion failure tied to the Windows CC runner's available memory and build parallelism settings; it is not reliably reproducible by re-running the same source on a differently-loaded runner.
recommended_actions: Reduce MSBuild/cl.exe parallelism for the Windows CC job (e.g., lower /MP or /cgthreads values, or cap maxcpucount) to keep the working set within the runner's available memory.
Evaluate moving the Windows Conditional Compilation job to a larger-memory Windows runner SKU.
Split the CC build into smaller parallel shards/targets so no single MSBuild invocation holds as many concurrent cl.exe processes.
Add automatic retry-with-reduced-parallelism for C1060 failures in the Windows CC workflow, since this is now a well-established recurring infra issue (26+ occurrences).
prevention_strategies: Track build-tool memory usage over time (vcxproj concurrency, cl.exe heap) and alert when parallelism settings exceed the known-safe envelope for the Windows CC runner SKU. Since this pattern already recurs dozens of times, treat it as a known infrastructure limitation and prioritize a durable fix (runner upsizing or parallelism cap) rather than re-investigating identical symptoms on each occurrence.
